title: 第三章 寻桩第七章 旧忆第八章 奠基
slug: 纳玄尘第五十三章安凌
content_zh:
又是三天过去了。
苏尘的身体已经恢复得七七八八。
武将世家的底子确实硬，昏迷七天七夜，养了不到一周，气色就回来了。脸色不再苍白，走路也有力气了，连王妃都不得不承认——这小子的恢复速度比她想象中快得多。
不过她依然坚持每天灌三碗补汤。
苏尘认了。
毕竟上辈子当太监的时候没人给他熬汤，这辈子有人关心，他没什么好抱怨的。
这天上午，苏尘独自坐在后院那棵银杏树下。
秋意更浓了。
满树金黄已经落了大半，地上铺了厚厚一层，踩上去沙沙响。阳光从稀疏的枝丫间漏下来，在石桌上投下斑驳的光影。
青萝被他支走了——他说想一个人待会儿。
实际上，他脑子里正在翻涌的，是曹钦留下的东西。
很庞大的东西。
曹钦临终前的记忆，在苏尘的脑海里像一本被翻开的档案册，每一页都写满了密密麻麻的内容——人名、地点、暗号、账簿、把柄、密道……
那些年，玄镜司的密报像潮水一样涌进曹钦的书房。他每天花两个时辰批阅，把每一条信息都记在脑子里，从不留纸面记录。
这是他的习惯。
也是他的保命之道。
你永远不知道哪一天，你写下的东西会成为别人手里捅向你的刀子。
苏尘闭着眼，细细梳理着那些记忆。
曹钦当年创立玄镜司的时候，明面上是“监察百官，肃清吏治”。
暗地里，他给自己留了一条后路。

他从不完全信任任何人——包括赵寒。
所以他在玄镜司的体系之外，另外设置了一套系统。
暗桩。
这些人都是玄镜司的底层人员或外围人员——街头的小贩、酒馆的跑堂、药铺的伙计、码头的搬运工……
他们不参与核心事务，甚至很多人根本不知道自己在为玄镜司做事。
他们只知道，有一个“督主”。
每隔一段时间，会有人通过特定的暗号与他们联系，传达指令，或者收取信息。
这些人，上绝对忠诚于曹钦个人——而不是玄镜司这个机构。
他们的存在，只有曹钦一个人知道。
连赵寒都不知道。
苏尘缓缓睁开眼，目光落在远处院墙的墙根处。
这些暗桩的联络方式，是一套极其精巧的暗号系统。
曹钦设计这套系统的时候，参考了他第一世在公职系统里学到的情报知识——结合这个世界的实际情况，做了因地制宜的改造。
每个暗桩都有一个固定的“联络点”。
这个点可能是某个店铺门口的石墩，也可能是一面青砖墙的特定角落，甚至是某棵树的树干。
暗桩会定期检查这个位置——看看上面有没有出现特定的记号。
记号的种类很多。
有时候是几道不起眼的刻痕，有时候是一个看似随意的涂鸦，有时候是一块放在特定位置的石头。
普通人路过根本不会注意，但暗桩一眼就能看懂。
记号传达的信息也很简单——通常是时间、地点、接头暗语。

如果暗桩在规定时间内看到了记号，就会在指定时间去指定地点，说出指定暗语，然后等待下一步指令。
如果没看到，就一切如常，该干嘛干嘛。
这套系统的精妙之处在于——它不需要任何居中联络人。
content_en:
Another three days passed.
Su Chen's body has recovered to some extent.
The background of a family of military commanders is indeed strong. He was in a coma for seven days and nights, and after less than a week, his complexion returned. His face was no longer pale and he had strength to walk. Even the princess had to admit that this boy's recovery was much faster than she imagined.
However, she still insists on taking three bowls of tonic soup every day.
Su Chen admitted it.
After all, no one made soup for him when he was a eunuch in his previous life. There are people who care about him in this life, so he has nothing to complain about.
This morning, Su Chen sat alone under the ginkgo tree in the backyard.
Autumn is getting stronger.
Most of the golden color on the trees has fallen, and there is a thick layer on the ground, which makes a rustling sound when you step on it. Sunlight leaked from the sparse branches, casting mottled light and shadow on the stone table.
Qingluo was taken away by him - he said he wanted to be alone for a while.
In fact, what was turbulent in his mind was what Cao Qin left behind.
Something huge.
Cao Qin's memories before his death were like an opened file in Su Chen's mind. Each page was filled with dense contents - names, locations, passwords, account books, handles, secret passages...
In those years, secret reports from the Xuanjing Division poured into Cao Qin's study like a tide. He spends two hours every day reviewing, keeping every piece of information in his mind and never leaving any paper records.
This is his habit.
It is also the way to save his life.
You never know one day what you write will become a knife stabbing you in someone else's hand.
Su Chen closed his eyes and carefully sorted through those memories.
When Cao Qin founded the Xuanjing Division, the apparent purpose was to "supervise all officials and eliminate the rule of officials."
Secretly, he left himself a way out.
He never completely trusts anyone - including Zhao Han.
So he set up another system in addition to Xuanjing Division's system.
Hidden piles.
These people are all low-level or peripheral personnel of Xuanjing Division - street vendors, tavern waiters, pharmacy clerks, dock porters...
They do not participate in core affairs, and many of them even do not know that they are working for Xuan Jingsi.
They only know that there is a "overlord".
Every once in a while, someone will contact them through a specific code to convey instructions or receive information.
These people are absolutely loyal to Cao Qin personally - not to the Xuanjing Division.
Only Cao Qin knew of their existence.
Even Zhao Han didn't know.
Su Chen slowly opened his eyes and his gaze fell on the base of the distant courtyard wall.
The contact information of these hidden stakes is an extremely sophisticated secret code system.
When Cao Qin designed this system, he referred to the intelligence knowledge he learned in the public service system in his first life - combined with the actual situation of the world, he made modifications based on local conditions.
Each hidden stake has a fixed "contact point".
This point may be a stone pier at the entrance of a certain shop, a specific corner of a brick wall, or even the trunk of a certain tree.
The hidden stake will periodically check this location to see if any specific marks appear on it.
There are many types of marks.
Sometimes it's a few inconspicuous carvings, sometimes it's a seemingly random graffiti, sometimes it's a stone placed in a specific location.
Ordinary people passing by would not notice it at all, but hidden piles can be seen at a glance.
The information conveyed by marks is also very simple-usually time, place, and joint code.
If the hidden stake sees the mark within the specified time, it will go to the specified place at the specified time, speak the specified code word, and then wait for the next instruction.
If you don't see it, it's business as usual and you do whatever you need to do.
The beauty of this system is that it doesn’t require any central contact.
